answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires an 18% cut the incumbent has refused to meet, and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so renewing as-is or negotiating further is unlikely to close the cost gap in time. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate and memory_c2 suggests past switches were smooth, but that memory was consolidated under different conditions than today's zero-buffer, 94%-of-committed-volume line. Given the objective explicitly forbids increasing delivery risk, a full cutover in 14 days is too risky to bet the whole primary supply on a single remembered success. I intend to initiate the vendor switch but constrain it to a small guarded test/phase-in against the current runway, verifying c2's original conditions (onboarding speed, invoicing accuracy claims) and c1's renewal stability record before committing further, since both bear directly on the risk-cost tradeoff this cycle.
